items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 46:1
items.html: In the surrounding lights there is no up and down, because in them both are equal; rather, the matter of inner and outer applies there, that the more inner is more inferior, and the more outer is more excellent. And the outer is more important than the inner circle, even when the outer is below the inner, as is known. Also, the discernment of the end and conclusion of the surrounding lights is at their center, as is known. Therefore, at the time when the second restriction was made, and the concluding Malchut, which had stood beneath the conclusion of the feet of AK, ascended to the place of the Bina of the body of the Partzuf TNHY of AK — and before the coupling Malchut ascended to the openings of the eyes, to couple with the upper light — the Chazeh and below of this Partzuf then fell to the discernment of the empty void of the first restriction, that is, beneath the conclusion of the feet of AK, in the place of the most inner circle, which is the closest to the central point, which is the empty void of the first restriction.
